column6: Writing to ducklake from spark via JDBC: each dataframe row becomes parquet file  I am planning to work with Ducklake from Apache Spark. Got initial ideas from a MotherDuck blog post about integrating Spark with DuckLake, which demonstrates using DuckDB to bootstrap DuckLake with a PostgreSQL metadata catalog and local Parquet files for data storage. The tutorial covers reading data via JDBC with smart partitioning and writing data back to DuckLake using Spark's DataFrame API.  First simple write attempt caused this question, here is code snippet (I used get_jdbc_writer() from above): rangeDf = spark.range(10) (     get_jdbc_writer(rangeDf)     .option('dbtable', "range_10")     .mode("overwrite")     .save() )  It worked but resulted in 10 parquet files in target directory. I checked - it is not related to partitions (rangeDf has one partition), if I change range() parameter to e.g. 4, I get 4 parquet files. I tried with bigger dataframe (several thousand rows) - the process never ended (too many files in directory, cannot even list them). This can be easily reproduced, initially I used older versions of DuckDB/Ducklake/JDBC. Is it a bug or is it "by design"?
